title: EV batteries last longer than drivers feared
gist: A study of over 500,000 tests across 20 popular EV models by Austria-based Aviloo found median battery state of health of 87-94 percent after 150,000 km, well above the 70 percent warranty floor, but with degradation varying widely by climate, battery size, and especially charging/parking habits — prompting UK EV groups to push for mandatory battery health certification standards.

themes.theme: Battery durability data undercuts a key EV adoption fear

insights.claim: Aviloo's study of more than 500,000 tests on 20 popular EV models, including Tesla's Model Y and Volkswagen's ID.4, found median state of health (SoH) between 87 percent and 94 percent after 150,000 km, comfortably above the 70 percent threshold that typically triggers a warranty replacement.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Directly counters a top consumer objection to EV purchases (battery degradation fear), which could support used-EV residual values and accelerate adoption if the finding gains broader consumer awareness.

insights.claim: EV battery warranties typically cover eight years or 100,000 miles (160,000 km), with manufacturers required to provide a replacement if capacity falls below 70 percent, and Aviloo's data shows most EVs are tracking well within that safety margin at comparable mileage.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete industry-standard warranty benchmark (70 percent floor, 8yr/100k-mile coverage) against which any EV battery health claim can be measured going forward.
insights.locator: EV battery warranties typically cover eight years

insights.claim: Median SoH across the 20 models studied was 91-97 percent after 50,000 km and 88-95 percent after 100,000 km, showing degradation is gradual and front-loaded rather than accelerating sharply with mileage within this tested range.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: The degradation curve shape (gradual, not a cliff) is useful for modeling used-EV valuation curves and residual-value assumptions at different mileage bands.
insights.locator: The median SoH was between 91 and 97 percent

themes.theme: Unlike combustion cars, an EV's real value depends on unseen usage history

insights.claim: Aviloo CEO Marcus Berger argues that unlike a combustion-engine car where age and mileage largely determine value and technical condition, two EVs of identical age and mileage can have very different battery health depending on how they were treated, meaning outward appearance no longer signals true condition.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Implies used-EV buyers face an information asymmetry problem that combustion-car buyers didn't, creating a market opening for battery-health certification and diagnostic services as a distinct value-add in used-EV transactions.
insights.quote: In contrast to a combustion engine car, where age and mileage would more or less carry the value of the car and technical condition, that's not the case for an EV
insights.locator: said Marcus Berger, chief executive of Aviloo

insights.claim: The speed of battery degradation varied significantly even within the same EV model depending on climate conditions, battery size, and driver habits such as parking behavior, with batteries in hotter climates degrading faster.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Climate is a material, non-controllable variable in battery longevity, meaning regional used-EV markets (e.g., hot climates) may command lower resale values or need adjusted warranty/insurance pricing.
insights.locator: also showed that the speed of battery degradation varied

insights.claim: Nissan's Leaf ZE1 showed the widest spread among the 20 models studied, with median SoH at 150,000 km varying by as much as 13.5 percentage points — equivalent to about 29 km of real-world range per charge — attributed partly to its smaller battery requiring more frequent charging.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Identifies the Nissan Leaf ZE1 as carrying the highest battery-health variance/risk among tested models, a specific data point for used-EV buyers or fleet operators evaluating that model versus peers.

insights.claim: Spread in battery health outcomes among individual cars of the same model reached up to 11 percentage points for Tesla's Model Y, 11-12 points for VW's ID.4, and more than 12 points for Hyundai's Ioniq 5.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Quantifies model-specific variance investors and used-car platforms can use to build risk-adjusted pricing or inspection requirements by brand/model.
insights.locator: Aviloo said the spread between the individual cars

insights.claim: Berger said very few consumers know that parking an EV with 100, 90, or 80 percent state of charge harms the battery, and that the ideal state of charge for parking is between 30 and 70 percent.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: A concrete, actionable consumer behavior rule (keep parked charge between 30-70 percent) that could materially affect resale value if adopted at scale, and a potential feature/education opportunity for automakers and fleet managers.
insights.quote: What very few consumers know is: don't park your cars with 100, 90, or 80 percent state of charge. It's just harming the battery.
insights.locator: Berger said batteries of EVs in hotter climates

themes.theme: Push for standardized battery health certification

insights.claim: Three of the UK's largest EV organizations recently called on the government to introduce mandatory battery health certifications to boost buyer confidence and reward owners who have properly maintained their vehicles.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: A potential regulatory catalyst: mandatory battery health certification, if adopted, would create a durable compliance/testing market (benefiting firms like Aviloo) and could reshape used-EV pricing transparency.
insights.locator: Aviloo's study came as three of the UK's largest EV organizations

insights.claim: Tesla UK's used-car sales and delivery manager James Strong said a nationally recognized battery state-of-health standard would strengthen confidence in the used EV market and improve transparency for consumers, indicating automaker-side support for standardized certification.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Automaker buy-in (Tesla UK) for standardized battery certification increases the likelihood such a standard could be adopted, which would reduce used-EV information asymmetry and potentially support resale values industry-wide.
insights.quote: We see the customer demand for confidence in battery health
insights.locator: said James Strong, used-car sales and delivery manager at Tesla UK

insights.claim: The Aviloo study notably did not include Chinese EV models due to a lack of available data.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: A data gap on Chinese EV battery durability (BYD and other major Chinese brands) limits how much this generally reassuring finding can be extrapolated to the fastest-growing segment of the global EV market.
insights.locator: The Aviloo study, which did not include Chinese models
